confessFirst.label: Communion Prayer before the priest's call
confessFirst.description: "I believe, O Lord…" precedes "In the fear of God…" rather than following it.

omitPreTrisagionLitany.label: Skip pre-Trisagion litany
omitPreTrisagionLitany.description: Goes from the third antiphon's exclamation directly to the Trisagion.

includeLesserSaints.label: Lesser-rank saint troparia on Sundays
includeLesserSaints.description: Saints ranked below "simple" are normally suppressed on Sundays; opt in to include them.

includeSecondGospel.label: Second Gospel reading
includeSecondGospel.description: When the day has two readings (e.g. polyeleos saint), both are read.

includeSecondKoinonikon.label: Second communion verse
includeSecondKoinonikon.description: When the day has two koinonika, both are sung.

omitCatechumensSeasons.label: Catechumens litanies — omit during
omitCatechumensSeasons.description: Seasons during which the Catechumens litanies are omitted. Comma-joined ids: paschal, lenten, bright-week.

paschalCommunionYearRound.label: Paschal communion hymn year-round
paschalCommunionYearRound.description: "Receive ye the Body of Christ" is sung outside the Paschal period as well.

beatitudesTropariaReaderLed.label: Reader-led Beatitudes troparia
beatitudesTropariaReaderLed.description: At the Third Antiphon, the Reader recites the canon troparia between Beatitude verses while the choir sings only the Beatitudes themselves. Common Slavic/Sluzhebnik practice.

faithful2Long.label: 2nd Litany of the Faithful — long form
faithful2Long.description: Deacon adds four great-litany-style petitions before "Help us, save us…". Older Russian-tradition Liturgika form; default is OCA Sluzhebnik short form.

hoursPrecedeService.label: Hours read before service (skip reader's opening prayers)
hoursPrecedeService.description: When Ninth Hour / Midnight Office is read immediately before Vespers or Matins, the reader's opening prayers (O Heavenly King → Trisagion → 12× Lord have mercy) were already said and are skipped. Service goes from the priest's exclamation directly to Psalm 103 (Vespers) or the royal opening (Matins).

licNoLeadingRepeat.label: Lord I Call — no leading sticheron repeat (9-count)
licNoLeadingRepeat.description: Saturday Great Vespers renders 9 stichera at Lord I Have Cried (6 octoechos verse-stichera + 3 menaion), not 10. Default behavior fills slot 7 by doubling sticheron 1, which OCA Obikhod publishes but parishes may read as a duplicate. The OCA Obikhod chant arrangement only supplies 6 verse-stichera per tone; this flag honors that count strictly. Glory/Now slots are unaffected.

defaultPronoun.label: Default language register (modern / traditional)
defaultPronoun.description: Register for variable hymn texts when a request does not specify ?pronoun. "yy" renders modern "You/Your" (thee/thou/thy and archaic verb forms are converted automatically); "tt" renders traditional "Thee/Thou". Applies to Vespers, Matins, and the Divine Liturgy. An explicit ?pronoun query param always overrides this default.

gloryAfterLittleLitany.label: “Glory to the Father” after the Little Litany
gloryAfterLittleLitany.description: The First Antiphon ends with its refrain, and “Glory to the Father…” is sung at the end of the Little Litany that follows, before Psalm 145. “Now and ever…” stays at the end of the Second Antiphon.
